These thresholds define whether a specific subsystem remains connected or is isolated during an abnormal condition. Accurate protection system modeling requires: • Implementation of protective relay logic with customizable thresholds for voltage, current, and frequency • Circuit breaker models supporting single-pole and three-pole operations, with realistic opening/closing time delays • Simulation of relay coordination and cascading trip sequences under various fault scenarios 13 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. • Integration of current transformer and voltage transformer saturation effects and harmonic filtering for refined fault discrimination. 3.8.1 Standard PSCAD Models Available PSCAD offers a range of protection system modeling elements, including circuit breakers, relays, and protective devices that can replicate fundamental protection functions, such as overcurrent, undervoltage, and distance protection. But it does so primarily through a combination of predefined components and user-defined or custom-built logic. 3.8.2 Additional Model Requirements Custom development is needed to incorporate: • Advanced relay functions, such as relay coordination—including timing, multizone protection, and cascading trip sequences—which are often implemented through user- developed logic or scripting • Communication-assisted protection features, such as breaker failure detection and interlocking • Breaker control and reclose sequences tailored to the operational requirements of data centers. 3.9 Higher-Level Control Systems Higher-level control systems in data centers include supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems, building management systems, energy management systems, paralleling switchgear controllers, and microgrid controllers, among others. These systems coordinate breaker operations and control distributed energy resources (DERs), loads, and backup generation to ensure reliable, efficient, and flexible operation. Incorporating supervisory control logic allows the assessment of how coordinated dispatch and automated restoration can mitigate widespread disconnections observed in past incidents. These control systems implement a complex sequence of operations to facilitate automated operation of the data center. Modeling of higher-level controls requires: • Implementation of custom control sequences for the operation of breakers, load/DER dispatch, and demand response • Real-time communication and monitoring interfaces between control layers and power equipment • Integration of fault detection, system isolation, and black-start control strategies. 3.9.1 Standard PSCAD Models Available PSCAD does not provide ready-made library models for higher-level data center control systems, such as microgrid controllers, SCADA systems, building automation systems, and energy management systems. Instead, models must be developed using custom logic and control blocks tailored to specific project requirements.
